newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST-SAfrica Nov CPI seen at 9.8 pct-economist.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-SAfrica Nov CPI seen at 9.8 pct-economist.

text.p: Consumer inflation was expected to rise to 9.8 percent year-on-year in November but would remain below 10 percent in December, Huysamer Stals economist Johan Rossouw said on Wednesday.
The October consumer price index (CPI) rose 9.1 percent year-on-year, according to Central Statistical Service data released earlier, which was 0.1 percentage point above Rossouw's own forecast.

The data was 0.4 percentage points above a Reuters consensus forecast of 8.8 percent and was fuelled by a 2.1 percent month-on-month increase in the food component. The non-food component grew 0.6 percent month-on-month or 8.2 percent from October last year.
Rossouw said he expected the food component to rise 2.1 percent again in November or 13.9 percent year-on-year, while the non-food component was expected to increase 0.7 percent month-on-month.
"Although the past two months' sharp increases in CPI spell higher inflation, it is still highly probable that by December 1996, CPI inflation will still be below 10 percent," Rossouw said.
CPI rose 8.4 percent year-on-year in September.
He added that inflation was expected to average at 7.5 percent for the year.
